front: What is E mail server in one sentence?
back: One-line: the MTA/MDA/MUA stack that accepts, routes, stores, and retrieves mail — debug deliverability at each hop.

front: Explain the mental model of E mail server (how the system thinks).
back: Email crosses distinct roles. Confusing them causes misconfigured ports and wrong logs.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for E mail server?
back: sudo systemctl status postfix → mailq → postqueue -p → postsuper -d ALL deferred # careful — deletes deferred queue → sudo tail -f /var/log/mail.log

front: Given a broken E mail server setup, what is your first validation command?
back: sudo systemctl status postfix

front: What are the production-safe defaults for E mail server?
back: [ ] A/AAAA for mail.example.com (SMTP banner host) [ ] MX points to MTA with priority [ ] SPF TXT includes all sending IPs/providers [ ] DKIM key published; MTA signs outbound [ ] DMARC policy (p=none → monitor, then quarantine/reject) [ ] PTR/rDNS matches SMTP EHLO hostname [ ] TLS cert valid for submission/IMAP hostnames

front: Symptom: Mail stuck in queue — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: mailq; defer reason in log · Fix: Fix DNS/MX; clear RBL; auth to smart host

front: Symptom: Users can't send — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: MSA auth / TLS · Fix: Verify SASL creds; cert chain on 587

front: Symptom: Users can't receive — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: MX DNS; MTA listening :25 · Fix: Fix MX; open SG; check postconf inet_interfaces

front: Symptom: IMAP works, no outbound — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Separate submission vs relay config · Fix: relayhost for smart host; SASL maps

front: Symptom: All mail spam-foldered — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SPF/DKIM/DMARC headers · Fix: See SMTP triage table

front: Symptom: Disk full — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: /var/spool/postfix; Maildir size · Fix: Expire queue; quota; expand volume

front: Symptom: Relay denied for world — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: smtpd_recipient_restrictions · Fix: permit_mynetworks, reject_unauth_destination

front: Symptom: TLS handshake fail on Apple Mail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Cert chain / intermediate · Fix: Install full chain; use Let's Encrypt

front: Gotcha with E mail server: what silently fails?
back: Open relay on port 25 = immediate blacklisting. Default Postfix is safe — custom mynetworks too wide is the usual mistake.

front: When should you NOT use E mail server?
back: Product email at scale → managed SMTP relay (SES, SendGrid) beats running your own MTA reputation. Dev-only fake SMTP → Mailhog/Mailpit locally; don't point at production MX.

front: What is IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) in one sentence?
back: One-line: mailbox protocol — messages stay on server; folders, flags, UID sync; clients use 143/STARTTLS or 993/IMAPS.

front: Explain the mental model of IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) (how the system thinks).
back: IMAP lets MUAs read and organize mail on the server (unlike POP3 (Post Office Protocol v3) which typically downloads and deletes). Server holds canonical state; client syncs flags (\Seen, \Deleted), folders, and UIDs. Multiple devices see the same mailbox.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol)?
back: Client ──IMAP──► MDA (Dovecot, Cyrus, Exchange) → openssl s_client -connect imap.example.com:993 -quiet → openssl s_client -connect imap.example.com:143 -starttls imap

front: Given a broken IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Client ──IMAP──► MDA (Dovecot, Cyrus, Exchange)

front: What are the production-safe defaults for IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol)?
back: STARTTLS on 143:

front: Symptom: Auth failed — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: App password; OAuth · Fix: Enable IMAP in provider; correct token scope

front: Symptom: Certificate error — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Hostname mismatch · Fix: Full SAN cert; use correct server name

front: Symptom: Empty INBOX on one client — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Wrong folder namespace · Fix: LIST folders; prefix INBOX

front: Symptom: Slow sync mobile — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: FETCH entire body · Fix: CONDSTORE/QRESYNC; partial FETCH

front: Symptom: IDLE disconnects — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NAT/firewall timeout · Fix: Client reconnect; TCP keepalive

front: Symptom: Messages "duplicate" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: POP3 + IMAP mixed · Fix: Pick one protocol per account

front: Symptom: Login plain rejected — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Secure auth required · Fix: TLS first; OAuth2

front: Gotcha with IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol): what silently fails?
back: PLAIN without TLS — credentials leak; always TLS or localhost.

front: When should you NOT use IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol)?
back: Offline-first archive download only — POP3 or one-shot migration tool simpler. Transactional app notifications — use webhooks/API, not mailbox polling.

front: What is MQTT in one sentence?
back: One-line: lightweight pub/sub for devices and IoT — broker-centric topics, QoS 0/1/2, small headers; not a drop-in for HTTP REST or chat at web scale without ops discipline.

front: Explain the mental model of MQTT (how the system thinks).
back: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) uses a broker (Mosquitto, EMQX, AWS IoT Core). Clients publish to topics (sensors/room1/temp); subscribers receive by topic filter (sensors/+/temp, # wildcard). Connection is long-lived TCP (often TLS on 8883).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for MQTT?
back: Publisher ──PUBLISH topic──► Broker ──forward──► Subscriber(s) → SUBSCRIBE filter → mosquitto_sub -h broker.example.com -p 8883 \ → mosquitto_pub -h broker.example.com -p 8883 \

front: Given a broken MQTT setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Publisher ──PUBLISH topic──► Broker ──forward──► Subscriber(s)

front: Symptom: Connect loop — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Auth/cert/clientId clash · Fix: Unique clientId; verify user/ACL

front: Symptom: Messages not received — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Topic typo vs filter · Fix: Log subscribe ack; test with mosquitto_sub -v

front: Symptom: Duplicate messages — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: QoS 1/2 retries · Fix: Idempotent handlers; dedupe by message id

front: Symptom: Broker CPU spike — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: # subscribers; retained flood · Fix: Narrow subscriptions; limit retain

front: Symptom: Silent disconnect — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NAT timeout · Fix: Keepalive (ping); broker max_keepalive

front: Symptom: TLS handshake fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: ALPN/SNI; old cipher · Fix: Update certs; mqtts:// not mqtt://

front: Gotcha with MQTT: what silently fails?
back: Plaintext 1883 on public internet — credentials + payload exposed; use TLS + ACL.

front: When should you NOT use MQTT?
back: Request/response HTTP APIs — REST/gRPC clearer for CRUD. Browser-first real-time — webSocket + app server may be simpler than MQTT-over-WS. Guaranteed global ordering — MQTT doesn't order across topics; design per-key streams.

front: What is Relay server?
back: A relay server is a server that forwards data between two or more devices or systems that cannot communicate directly.

front: What is Proxy Servers?
back: Allow the device to access external services (like TURN) even when outgoing traffic is restricted.

front: What is WebSocket/HTTP TURN?
back: Increases the chances of traffic being allowed through the firewall by using protocols that are more commonly permitted.

front: What is VPN?
back: Bypasses firewall restrictions by tunneling traffic through a secure connection.

front: What is SCP (Secure Copy Protocol) in one sentence?
back: One-line: file copy over SSH — reuses sshd auth and encryption; prefer rsync -e ssh or SFTP for large/recursive transfers with resume.

front: Explain the mental model of SCP (Secure Copy Protocol) (how the system thinks).
back: SCP wraps SSH transport: authenticate like ssh, then copy files over encrypted channel. Syntax mirrors cp with remote user@host:path. Not a separate daemon — sshd on port 22 (or custom).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for SCP (Secure Copy Protocol)?
back: local scp ──SSH session──► sshd ──► read/write remote files → scp file.txt user@remote_host:/path/to/destination/ → scp -r ./local_dir user@remote_host:/remote/path/ → scp user@remote_host:/path/to/file.txt ./local/ → scp -r user@remote_host:/remote/dir ./local/

front: Given a broken SCP (Secure Copy Protocol) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: local scp ──SSH session──► sshd ──► read/write remote files

front: Symptom: Permission denied (publickey) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SSH key agent · Fix: ssh-add -l; correct -i key; authorized_keys

front: Symptom: Host key verification failed — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Known_hosts mismatch · Fix: Verify fingerprint; update known_hosts carefully

front: Symptom: Stalled mid-transfer — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Network drop · Fix: Use rsync; ServerAliveInterval in ssh config

front: Symptom: scp: not found — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Remote no scp binary · Fix: Use sftp/rsync; install openssh-clients on remote

front: Symptom: Wrong owner on remote — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Remote umask · Fix: scp preserves modes; fix with ssh chmod after

front: Symptom: Slow many small files — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Per-file overhead · Fix: tar+scp one archive, or rsync

front: Gotcha with SCP (Secure Copy Protocol): what silently fails?
back: Glob expansion is local — scp *.log host: expands on local shell; quote remote globs: host:'/logs/*.log'.

front: When should you NOT use SCP (Secure Copy Protocol)?
back: Large dataset sync with resume — rsync over SSH. Public anonymous download — HTTPS/S3, not SCP. Windows ↔ Linux path quirks — verify OpenSSH build; consider SFTP GUI clients.

back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: local scp ──SSH session──► sshd ──► read/write remote files

front: What is SMTP in one sentence?
back: One-line: push protocol for MTA-to-MTA mail relay — submission on 587/TLS, legacy 25, implicit TLS 465 — RFC 5321.

front: Explain the mental model of SMTP (how the system thinks).
back: SMTP is command/response between mail agents. Submission (client → MSA, port 587) differs from relay (MTA → MTA, port 25). Delivery authenticity is enforced separately via SPF, DKIM, DMARC (DNS TXT) — not by SMTP itself.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for SMTP?
back: MUA ──587/TLS──► MSA/MTA ──25──► recipient MTA ──► MDA ──► mailbox → SPF/DKIM/DMARC checked at recipient → openssl s_client -connect smtp.example.com:587 -starttls smtp → swaks --to rcip@example.com --from sender@example.com \ → dig +short example.com TXT # SPF

front: Given a broken SMTP setup, what is your first validation command?
back: MUA ──587/TLS──► MSA/MTA ──25──► recipient MTA ──► MDA ──► mailbox

front: What are the production-safe defaults for SMTP?
back: Example SPF: v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ip4:203.0.113.0/24 -all

front: Symptom: Mail lands in spam — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Authentication-Results header; mail-tester.com · Fix: Fix SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment; warm IP; reverse PTR

front: Symptom: 550 5.7.1 SPF fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: dig TXT example.com; sending IP · Fix: Add IP/include to SPF; avoid -all until complete

front: Symptom: 550 5.7.1 DKIM fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Selector TXT; signed headers · Fix: Re-sign with correct selector; clock skew on signer

front: Symptom: DMARC fail in aggregate report — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: From domain vs DKIM d= vs SPF bounce domain · Fix: Align domains (envelope From = Header From); use same domain for DKIM

front: Symptom: Connection timed out on :25 — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Cloud SG blocks outbound 25 · Fix: Request provider unblock or relay via SES/SendGrid

front: Symptom: Relay access denied — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Auth required on 587 · Fix: Enable SASL; credentials in MUA

front: Symptom: 421 4.7.0 try again — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Greylisting / rate limit · Fix: Retry; fix reputation; reduce burst volume

front: Symptom: Works to Gmail, not corporate — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Recipient MX logs / TLS requirement · Fix: Offer TLS 1.2+; valid cert on submission

front: Symptom: Bounces with 550 5.1.1 — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: RCPT address valid? · Fix: Fix typo; verify MX for domain

front: Symptom: Queue backlog — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: mailq / postqueue -p · Fix: Clear deferred; fix DNS; unblock RBL listing

front: Gotcha with SMTP: what silently fails?
back: SPF -all before all senders listed → all mail fails. Use ~all during migration, then tighten.

front: When should you NOT use SMTP?
back: App transactional at scale → provider API (SES, Postmark) beats self-hosted MTA ops. Internal alerts only → Slack/webhook may beat email deliverability fight.

back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: MUA ──587/TLS──► MSA/MTA ──25──► recipient MTA ──► MDA ──► mailbox

front: What is SOCKS (Socket Secure) in one sentence?
back: One-line: client-side proxy protocol that tunnels arbitrary TCP (and UDP in v5) through a proxy — debug egress and bypass paths — RFC 1928.

front: Explain the mental model of SOCKS (Socket Secure) (how the system thinks).
back: Unlike HTTP proxies (URL-level), SOCKS hands the client a tunnel after authentication. The client then speaks the target protocol raw — SSH, HTTPS, DB, anything TCP.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for SOCKS (Socket Secure)?
back: App ──SOCKS handshake──► Proxy (:1080) ──TCP connect──► target:443 → ssh -N -D 1080 -q user@jump-host → curl --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:1080 https://ifconfig.me → curl -v --proxy socks5h://127.0.0.1:1080 https://internal.service.local → nc -X 5 -x 127.0.0.1:1080 target.host 443

front: Given a broken SOCKS (Socket Secure) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: App ──SOCKS handshake──► Proxy (:1080) ──TCP connect──► target:443

front: Symptom: Connection refused to SOCKS port — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: ss -tlnp; SSH -D running? · Fix: Start tunnel; open firewall to jump host

front: Symptom: Works for IP, fails for hostname — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SOCKS4 vs SOCKS5; DNS local vs remote · Fix: Use socks5h:// (remote resolve) not socks5://

front: Symptom: Auth failure — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Username/password required · Fix: curl -U user:pass --socks5-hostname ...

front: Symptom: Tunnel up, target timeout — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Proxy can't reach destination · Fix: SG on target; routing from jump host; wrong VPC

front: Symptom: HTTPS cert errors through tunnel — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Expected if MITM corporate proxy · Fix: Use corporate CA; not a SOCKS bug

front: Symptom: Intermittent drops — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Idle NAT timeout on jump path · Fix: Enable SSH ServerAliveInterval 60

front: Symptom: UDP apps fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SOCKS4 or no UDP associate · Fix: SOCKS5 with UDP relay; many tools TCP-only

front: Gotcha with SOCKS (Socket Secure): what silently fails?
back: socks5 vs socks5h: Without h, DNS resolves locally — leaks intent and breaks internal-only names. Prefer -hostname / socks5h:// for tunnel debugging.

front: When should you NOT use SOCKS (Socket Secure)?
back: Terminate TLS and inspect HTTP → HTTP CONNECT or explicit forward proxy, not raw SOCKS. Permanent service mesh routing → use sidecar/iptables, not manual -D tunnels.

back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: App ──SOCKS handshake──► Proxy (:1080) ──TCP connect──► target:443

front: What is TFTP?
back: TFTP is a simple file transfer protocol that transfers files over a network using UDP instead of TCP. It is designed for environments where devices need to download or upload files with minimal protocol overhead.
